article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: No games today, Thursday's starter is set, four Baltimore starters are back to full practice, and the Thursday line has ticked to 10 at one book while the app board still shows Week 8.

items.headline: Lead: No games today — Thursday is the next game, and the board has not caught up yet
paragraphs: There are no NFL games today, Wednesday, November 4. The next game is Jacksonville at Baltimore on Thursday, November 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET.

Read the board plainly: the app still shows Week 8, generated November 2, with no Week 9 cards at all. That means the app has not picked up Joe Fagnano as Thursday's starter yet — its Week 8 Baltimore game still shows the quarterback as unresolved. Do not look to the board for Thursday's quarterback; the practice reports below are the current word.
The inactive list lands about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday. If anything changes there, that is the last check before you act on a Thursday price.
items.takeaway: No games today; Thursday is Jacksonville at Baltimore at 8:15 p.m. ET, and the app board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards.

items.headline: Injury roundup: four Baltimore starters back to full practice, Tuten still has not practiced
paragraphs: Baltimore's quarterback picture is unchanged and settled: undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will make his first career start Thursday. He was a full participant Tuesday with his right ankle heavily taped and braced after hurting it Sunday at Buffalo, where he finished 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception and a lost fumble. Lamar Jackson did not practice with his right thumb injury and is headed for surgery and injured reserve. Tyler Huntley did not practice with his toe injury and is out for Thursday.

The better news for Baltimore is on the lines and at linebacker: offensive linemen Vega Ioane and Ronnie Stanley, linebacker Roquan Smith, outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, and running back Justice Hill were all upgraded from limited to full participation Tuesday. Kicker Tyler Loop was placed on injured reserve Tuesday with a groin injury, so Jake Moody is expected to kick Thursday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins did not practice with a knee injury. Starting right guard Roger Rosengarten (ankle), starting left guard John Simpson (back), and nose tackle John Jenkins (knee) were limited both days of practice this week.

For Jacksonville, running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice Monday or Tuesday with ankle and foot injuries, and his status for Thursday is in question. Whether he practices Wednesday is the next signal. Chris Rodriguez Jr. was limited both days with a hand injury, and defensive end Travon Walker went from not practicing Monday to limited Tuesday with a rib injury. Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton (torn quadriceps) and safety Eric Murray (elbow) are out for the season and headed to injured reserve.
items.takeaway: Fagnano starts Thursday with a braced ankle; four Baltimore starters returned to full practice, Loop is on injured reserve, and Tuten has missed two straight practices.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The cards on the board are Monday's history, not live picks
paragraphs: The only cards on the board are Monday night's, and that game is over. Hit Rate was Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings — the pick the app rates most likely to win, which forgoes value for win probability. Seattle lost, so that pick lost. Balanced and Value were both Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings, and Chicago won outright, so that pick won.

Say it straight: Hit Rate is the likeliest pick, not a promise, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much — a good starting point for a new bettor. Value is always the model's +EV play. None of them is deficient for being a different kind of pick; they answer different questions.

When the board flips to Week 9, Thursday's cards will appear. Until then, if your book already has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override — and it is the right tool here, because the board itself has not picked up Thursday's quarterback yet.
items.takeaway: Monday's cards are history — Hit Rate lost, Balanced and Value won — and until the board flips to Week 9, run any Thursday price through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: what a key number is
paragraphs: A key number is a final margin that games land on more often than other margins. In football, 3 and 7 matter most, because so many games end on a field goal or a touchdown with the extra point.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you like a favorite, and you can bet that team at -3. If the team wins by exactly 3, a -3 bet pushes and your stake comes back. But if the line moves to -3.5 before you bet, that same 3-point win loses. The team did not change. The number did.
That is why bettors watch half-points around key numbers so closely. Getting -2.5 instead of -3, or +7.5 instead of +7, can turn a loss into a push or a push into a win.
items.takeaway: Key numbers are the margins games land on most, so a half-point across 3 or 7 changes the bet even when the team does not change.

items.headline: Thursday's line has ticked to 10 at one book, and the total is down to 40
paragraphs: This is all one move, and it is still the quarterback story. The shadow-tracked lookahead had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5. By Tuesday morning it had flipped to Jacksonville favored by 8.5 to 9.5 points with the total at 42.5, and Tuesday evening FanDuel listed Jacksonville -9.5 with a total of 40.5.

This morning's snapshot, updated 7:58 a.m. ET, shows the move stretching a little further: Jacksonville -9.5 at BetRivers, Baltimore +10 at Fanatics, with the total at Over 40 at Fanatics and Under 40.5 at Hard Rock Bet. The moneyline is Jacksonville -500 at BetRivers and Baltimore +400 at DraftKings.

The app has not caught this move yet — its board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, with no Week 9 cards at all. So do not look to the board for Thursday's price. If your book has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Baltimore -3 and a 48.5 total in the lookahead are long gone — Jacksonville is now a 9.5- to 10-point favorite with the total at 40 to 40.5.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The quarterback question is answered, so there is no reason to wait on that news anymore. If your book has a Thursday number you like, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
The one thing still worth waiting on is the inactive list, about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday. If anything changes there, run your price through Check again before you act.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here. Settlement in the tracker is manual, and it only works if you are honest with yourself — log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Thursday game? Thursday check. Run your book's Thursday price through Check now, and re-check if the inactive list changes anything.
